text.p: These are the main stories in Lithuanian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that three major Mafia groups in Lithuania, one in Kaunas and two in Vilnius, previously enjoyed the support of high ranking political and legal officials.
- The ambassador of the European Commission delegation in Lithuania, Henrik Schmiegelow, said in an interview that Lithuania should make more effort to promote its positive developments.
- Beer production in Lithuania increased by 12 percent in April compared to March.

- Direct foreign investment in Lithuania was 2.287 billion litas as of January 1, 1997. The biggest foreign investor was the United States at 663 million litas. German companies have invested 301 million litas in the country.
- The chief prosecutor of Vilnius, Rimantas Grockis, submitted his letter of resignation on Thursday to the prosecutor general.
- The Lithuanian Prime Minister said on Thursday that only 1.25 million people pay taxes to the Social insurance fund SODRA compared to 1.9 million a few years ago.
- The international theatre festival LIFE starts in Vilnius on Friday with the premier of Hamlet directed by Eimuntas Nekroshius.
- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said that inflation during the second quarter of the year was expected to be 2.4 percent compared to 3.5 percent during first three months of the year.

- The Lithuanian government made an attempt to regulate salaries of the employees of the three state-run banks. This move might lead to the loss of the top people in the banks, the head of the Bankers' Association, Eduardas Vilkelis, said.
- Pepsi Cola General Bottlers launches an aggressive advertising campaign Pepsi Force and intends to invest $50 million in the next five years into the Baltic countries.
- The Lithuanian government decided to reorganise Lithuanian Telecom into a joint-stock company.
